html:
The Miyan were an Aboriginal Australian people of inland central Queensland, in the country west of the coastal ranges behind Mackay. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Almost nothing is recorded of them beyond their name and the rough bounds of their land. Neighbours on the map include the Yilba, the Yambina, the Yangga and the Yagalingu. Sheep and cattle runs spread across this country in the 1860s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
